newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy shares close lower in wave of profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Italy shares close lower in wave of profit-taking.

text.p: Italian shares closed lower across the board on Tuesday with a few exceptions, notably information technology group Olivetti, which ended up on a spate of buying spurred by the sale of its PC business to a group of foreign and Italian investors.
The all-share mibtel index finished 0.89 percent down at 12,224 while the blue-chip mib30 closed 0.9 percent down at 18,322. Olivetti closed 1.67 percent higher at 675 lire.
"We are looking for more profit-taking," said a Milan based equities salesman. "People are getting used to these new higher levels and don't reckon the market has much further to go at the moment."
Olivetti opened well up at 705 lire on news of the sale, which was announced on Monday evening after the markets had closed, before edging lower at the close.
"Olivetti held up well but if the sale had been announced last week when the market was rising it would probably have gone limit-up," said a Milan-based stockbroker.
Analysts described the round of profit-taking as a technical correction. Domestic institutional buyers, who have helped drive the increases of the past fortnight, were also scarce.
Among the few strong gainers was investment bank IMI, which put on 1.84 percent to close at 15,900 lire. The bank is seen benefiting from the switch by many investors into equity mutual funds.
The market recovered some ground shortly before the close on Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's favourable copmments about the U.S. economy which helped lift the dollar and Wall Street.
